wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Tiberius A.ii
wormald.wormald_origin: Gospel-book given by King Æthelstan to Christ Church Canterbury, with an inscription by the charter scribe Chaplais calls ‘Scribe (3)’ (p. 169 and n. 25); its charters are for Canterbury cathedral (p. 191).
wormald.other_contents: Gospel-book which once contained charters, writs and property memoranda for Christ Church Canterbury; Cotton moved the Old English ones (seven + one pages, including a spurious Latin/OE pancarta of Æthelred II and a grant by a Thored) to Claudius A.iii and most Latin (papal) ones to Faustina B.vi (p. 191 and n. 117; p. 192).
wormald.overview: A Canterbury Gospel-book, given to Christ Church by King Æthelstan, from which Cotton cut its Canterbury charters, putting the English ones at the front of Claudius A.iii (where they sit beside VI Æthelred) and most of the papal ones in Faustina B.vi. Cotton may have chosen this arrangement because he thought Tiberius A.ii was the book on which kings swore at their coronation. The transplanted grant by a Thored once misled scholars into assigning the VI Æthelred pontifical to Canterbury.
wormald.key_quote: 'taken from the Gospel-book now Cotton Tiberius A.ii' (p. 191)
wormald.doubts: Not in the guide as a separate item; relevant because the guide's K description (Canterbury gospel book with OE charters) refers to these transplanted leaves. Contains no laws.
verify_notes: Added (pp. 169 and n. 25) that it was Æthelstan’s gift to Christ Church; pages extended.
overview: reworded to remove five-word runs matching Wormald’s text.
